revisionReason: Declare unsupported-controller-state-after-approval in the data-plane and both migration phases. Both resource families and database engines introduce only a future stored execution-binding version after approval and manager startup. The shipping controller contract remains 1. A private name-scoped status PATCH grant preserves installed admission, grants the real manager nothing, and is removed by exact UID with an effective-permission denial control. The runtime proof requires distinct exact refusal reconciliations, unchanged full status and spec, closed resource and workload histories through natural EOF, an unconsumed exact original approval, native diagnostic SQL controls and no unauthorized SQL. Withdrawal precedes restoration of version 1, and a fresh approval must produce one exact Apply with native database effects. This measures unsupported restored input, not compatibility with a future state contract. All eight frozen source hashes, operating limits, alert targets, RPO/RTO and the 30 required cells are unchanged. Local unit, race, tagged compilation and static checks supply no runtime acceptance. The scenario requires final artifact execution; runner-protocol and lifecycle proofs and the remaining qualification issues stay open.
